sentence: A 70-year-old man with neuralgia of the pudendal nerve secondary to a direct injury following a trans-ureteral resection of the prostate (TUR-P).
He reported pain with neuropathic characteristics (burning, paresthesia) in the external genitalia.
Of severe intensity (VAS 10/10), associated with pain when defecating and urinating, which was relieved after the act.

As a first measure in the unit, after 5 years of pain, pharmacological therapy was started with carbamazepine (200 mg/d), pregabalin (150 mg/12 hours), amitriptyline (25 mg/nightly) and tramadol (200 mg/day).

Due to lack of response to pharmacological treatment, following the protocol of the previous cases, depression and mild anxiety are reported in the Beck depression questionnaire and the Goldberg health questionnaire, which do not contraindicate the placement of the device, so CENPP is carried out in September 2014.
Symptomatic improvement was obtained, so NERSR was implemented.
He presented a complication due to a CSF fistula, which resolved in the sixth week with conservative management.
One month after treatment, the patient was pain-free.
Currently, the patient has 100% coverage without oral medications.
Beck's depression questionnaire and Goldberg's health questionnaire with mild anxiety without data on depression.
